body:
Upstream issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/32158

Mirror issue: https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/2123

## What changed

- Changed scheduler load accounting to inspect every `running_mbs` slot when pipeline parallelism is enabled, while retaining the existing singleton `running_batch` behavior without PP.
- Counted unique request IDs across slots so overlapping references cannot inflate the reported load.
- Added a failing-before/passing-after CPU regression for distributed PP slots, cross-slot deduplication, and singleton/empty boundary cases.
- Added the required investigation report and raw evidence under `reports/j-0b3781ed1483/`.

## Reproduction and validation

On base commit `358c163250ad3b1f62939b01ce1314a0a31a0365`, the new regression failed because `SchedulerLoadInquirer` could only read the currently selected `running_batch`. With this commit:

```text
/tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-0b3781ed1483/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_v1_loads_aggregate.py test/registered/unit/managers/scheduler_components/test_load_inquirer.py
8 passed
```

All pre-commit hooks for the changed and reported files also pass.

## Limitations

The assigned environment exposes one AMD Instinct MI350X (`gfx950`) GPU. The reported TP=2, PP=4 deployment requires eight GPUs, and model weights were not supplied, so I did not run or claim the original 16-request multi-GPU HTTP reproduction. The regression exercises the actual CPU-side scheduler accounting path and does not validate pipeline communication or full-model execution. No native source changed, so no native rebuild was performed.
